lines.text: He had been at his new school for exactly one week, when they called him a thief.
It started with notes. The teacher told the class to borrow notes from the other class, to complete their own.
He borrowed one from a girl in the other class.
The next day, during break, while he was outside, she slipped into his class and took her note back from his bag.
After break, he checked his bag. Her note was gone.
His classmates told him who took it.
That girl from the other class came during break and took it!
So he went to her class, just to be sure.
Yes, I took it back. It's my note.
Later that same day, she burst into his class.
My money is gone! Somebody stole my money!
He was the only outsider who had been in her class that day. So everyone turned to him.
They searched his bag. Inside, exactly the amount she lost.
He stayed calm.
What bills were they?
Just one bill. A twenty.
He smiled, and pulled out two tens.
Then you changed it! You are still a thief!
The teachers came. They searched his pockets, and found even more money.
Where did a new boy get all this? You stole from home too!
Then the school president, the biggest boy in the whole school, leaned in.
Thief.
In the principal's office, they finally called his father.
Sir, how much did you give your son today?
Thirty dollars. Two tens for lunch, and ten for the bus.
Exactly what was in his bag, and his pocket. The room went silent.
A week later, the truth came out. Another girl in his class had taken her money, just to teach her a lesson.
